title: EduTrack

summary.en: A K-5 planning-tool concept unifying long-range lesson planning, the daily teaching hour and standards tracking into one Plan → Do → Review rhythm, styled like a paper planbook rather than a dashboard. Lessons are physical index cards dragged onto days. Built as a live prototype with drag-and-drop lesson cards.
summary.jp: 教師は年間計画も日々の授業も基準管理もしている。ただ 3 つがつながっていない。1 つのリズムでつなぐ構想を考えた。紙の教案帳のような操作感で試作した。

product.en: The insight wasn't a missing feature but a missing rhythm: teachers already plan, teach and track standards, but nothing connects the three. One Plan → Do → Review tool, built to feel like the paper planbook it replaces rather than a new dashboard to learn.
product.jp: 足りなかったのは機能でなくリズムだった。教師はすでに計画し、教え、基準を記録しているが、3 つをつなぐ仕組みがない。紙の教案帳の手触りのまま、1 つの流れに束ねた。

mine: Designed a single tool tying long-range planning, daily teaching and standards coverage together via a Plan → Do → Review rhythm
Designed lessons as physical index cards that get dragged onto days
Set the visual language as 'a planbook, not a dashboard' — warm paper surfaces, square corners, shadow depth
Built a live prototype as the source of truth for the design system, plus a companion storybook
team: Domain Expert (Education), UX Researcher and Developer — credited on the page by role title, without individual task breakdown

label.jp: 計画・実行・振り返りの 3 工程

narrative.problem: A classroom teacher plans a whole school year in a paper planbook, tracks standards in a district spreadsheet, and runs each day from memory or a sticky note. Nothing connects the plan to what actually gets taught, or to whether the standards were ever covered.
built: Companion Storybook documenting the design system

_notes: Concept-stage project; no client named and no adoption/impact metrics stated on the page.
Engagement not explicitly stated; recorded as unstated rather than assumed.
